samples.summary: Comment author is `username: undefined` for every API-key caller (the primary consumer of these routes)
samples.evidence: `author()` builds `{ userId: String(req.user.id), username: req.user.username }`. For API-key auth the request user comes from `packages/backend/src/api-key/api-key.strategy.ts:22-27`, which returns only `{ id, workspaceId, scopes, isApiKey }` — there is no `username` (only the JWT strategy sets one, `packages/backend/src/auth/jwt.strategy.ts:39-44`). So every thread/reply/resolve made with an API key (the CLI/agent path this feature exists for) writes `username: undefined` into the CRDT. Yorkie rejects `undefined` values on assignment, so this is likely a 500 on the write; if it does get stored, every API-authored comment and `resolvedBy` renders with no author in the editor. The controller docblock claims "an API key resolves to the user who minted it" — only the id does; the username is never loaded from the user table.

samples.summary: `copyThread` shallow-spreads the anchor, so nested CRDT proxies (PDF `rect`, docs `posRange`) leak into the HTTP response instead of plain JSON
samples.evidence: `anchor: { ...t.anchor } as AnyAnchor` copies nested values by reference. For a PDF thread the anchor is `{ kind, pageIndex, rect: {...} }` and for a docs thread `{ blockId, posRange, quotedText }` — the nested objects stay live Yorkie proxies. The repo's own equivalents avoid exactly this: `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:51-70` ("a spread would carry live proxy objects out of the CRDT, which is the bug this whole copy layer exists to prevent") copies field by field, and `packages/backend/src/api/v1/worksheet-charts.controller.ts:61-72` documents that a spread makes `res.json()` fail or double-encode. This fires on `GET /comments` (list), `PATCH /comments/:id` and the reply/resolve responses for pdf and doc documents — i.e. the anchor a client needs to place the thread comes back double-encoded or crashes serialization. The sheet-cell anchor (flat strings) is unaffected, which is why the unit tests miss it.

samples.summary: `unwrapJson` on a whole worksheet uses bare `JSON.parse`, so duplicating a tab whose grid contains a control character (a multi-line cell) throws a 500
samples.evidence: `const worksheet = unwrapJson<Worksheet>(root.sheets?.[tabId]);` — `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:7-19) calls the proxy's `toJSON()` and then plain `JSON.parse`. The same file documents that Yorkie's raw JSON string path emits *unescaped control characters inside string values*, which is precisely why `parseJsonSnapshot`/`escapeControlCharsInJson` (lines 93-110) exist. A cell value containing a newline or tab is ordinary spreadsheet content, so `POST /tabs/:tabId/duplicate` would throw `SyntaxError` out of the withDocument callback and 500 instead of duplicating. Previous `unwrapJson` call sites only unwrapped small chart/image records; this is the first one that unwraps an entire user-authored grid.

samples.summary: Every per-slide op replaces the whole `root.slides` array, so concurrent edits to *any* slide between read and write are lost — the opposite of what the docblock claims
samples.evidence: `apply()` reads the deck (`readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())`), computes a new array outside `doc.update`, then assigns `root.slides = result.slides` wholesale. Yorkie resolves that as last-write-wins over the entire array, discarding any element/text change a collaborator committed on any slide in the interval. The class docblock says these verbs "each rewrite only `root.slides`" so "every concurrent edit in between" is preserved — only edits to `meta`/`themes`/`layouts` are. `writeSlidesRoot` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/slides-tree.ts:83-92) states the destructive contract explicitly; this path silently inherits it while documenting the opposite.

samples.summary: An unknown `layoutId` is silently substituted with the first built-in layout instead of being rejected
samples.evidence: `add` accepts any non-empty `layoutId` string and passes it to `slide-ops.addSlide` → `MemSlidesStore.addSlide` → `resolveLayout` → `getLayout(layoutId)`, which is `BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS.find(...) ?? BUILT_IN_LAYOUTS[0]` (packages/slides/src/model/layout.ts:196-198). A typo'd or stale layout id therefore creates a slide with the wrong layout and a `layoutId` the caller never asked for, with a 200 response that does not report which layout was used — the exact failure the new `GET /layouts` catalog exists to prevent. No `not_found` result is produced for layouts, unlike for slide ids.

samples.summary: Lazy creation of the `comments` map re-introduces the concurrent-first-comment data loss the model explicitly warns about
samples.evidence: `if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}` (sheet path) and `if (!root.comments) root.comments = {}` (pdf path, line 195). `packages/sheets/src/model/workbook/worksheet-document.ts:157-164` seeds `comments: {}` at worksheet creation precisely because "If the map were instead created lazily on first comment (`if (!ws.comments) ws.comments = {}`), two users adding the first comment concurrently would each create a fresh map and one — with its thread — would be dropped wholesale." On a legacy worksheet without the seeded map, an API-created thread races a concurrent editor-created thread and one is lost.

samples.summary: PDF rect validation checks each component in 0..1 but never `x+w <= 1` / `y+h <= 1`, so a rectangle wholly off the page is accepted
samples.evidence: `parsePdfAnchor` loops `['x','y','w','h']` requiring each in `[0,1]`. `{ x: 0.9, y: 0.9, w: 0.9, h: 0.9 }` passes and stores an anchor whose region extends past the page edge; the viewer will draw a highlight that is mostly off-page. It also accepts `w: 0`/`h: 0`, a zero-area anchor with no clickable target. The unit test only covers `w: 2`, which the per-component check happens to catch.

samples.summary: A1 anchor validation accepts references with a zero/garbage row, because `parseRef` does not validate the numeric part
samples.evidence: `parseRef(anchor)` is used purely as a throws/doesn't-throw check. `parseRef` (packages/sheets/src/model/core/coordinates.ts:323-348) only requires a digit somewhere after position 0: `"A0"` yields row 0, `"A1B2"` yields row 1, and a lowercase `"b2"` yields column 34 (`charCodeAt('b') - 65 + 1`). All of these are stored verbatim as an image anchor, placing the image off-grid or on a silently different cell than the caller named.

samples.summary: `reply` and `setResolved` return a sheet thread without the derived `ref`, unlike `list` and `createThread`
samples.evidence: `createThread` (line 220) and `list` (line 137) pass the thread through `withSref` to attach the derived A1 `ref`; `mutateThread`, used by `reply` and `setResolved`, returns `copyThread(thread)` unchanged. The same thread therefore has an anchor with `ref` on some responses and without it on others, so a client that reads `anchor.ref` gets `undefined` after resolving a thread.

verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described. `author()` (comments.controller.ts:105-112) reads `req.user.username`, but the API-key principal (api-key.strategy.ts:22-27) contains only `{id, workspaceId, scopes, isApiKey}` — only jwt.strategy.ts:39-44 sets a username, and neither CombinedAuthGuard (combined-auth.guard.ts:16-26), WorkspaceScopeGuard (workspace-scope.guard.ts:32-46) nor ApiKeyWriteScopeGuard (api-key-write-scope.guard.ts:38-49) enriches the user, so no guard makes this unreachable: a write-scoped key reaches createThread/reply/setResolved. comment-ops.ts:45-49 unconditionally copies `username: a.username` into the object written into the CRDT, while CommentAuthor.username is a required string (packages/sheets/src/comment/types.ts:1-5). Result on the API-key path is either a throw inside doc.update (500) or an authorless comment/resolvedBy stored in the CRDT; both are wrong behavior on a normally reachable path. Existing tests only cover a JWT-shaped user (comments.controller.spec.ts:11), and the controller docblock (line 76-78) asserts the API key "resolves to the user who minted it", which only holds for the id. No named refutation ground applies.

The anchors involved are nested (`pdf-region` -> `rect` object at comments.controller.ts:450; `pdf-text` -> `rects` array at pdf-comment-store.ts:57-63; docs -> `posRange` per comments.controller.ts:174-178), so those nested values stay live Yorkie proxies. This repo documents the consequence itself: yorkie-json.ts:1-6 (proxy `toJSON` returns a JSON *string*, so spread/stringify double-encode), worksheet-charts.controller.ts:61-72 (`{ ...proxy }` puts a nested proxy in the response where `res.json()` dies), and pdf-comment-store.ts:51-55 (field-by-field copy precisely because "a spread would carry live proxy objects out of the CRDT"). Reachable on normal paths: `copyThread` receives live proxies at comments.controller.ts:150 (GET /comments for doc/pdf), :136 (sheet list), and :364 (mutateThread, used by PATCH resolve and reply) — only the POST pdf path (:198) passes a plain object. No global response interceptor normalizes the payload. Tests only exercise flat sheet-cell anchors (comment-ops.spec.ts:27,71-72), so they miss it. Wrong/unusable anchor data on a normal-use read path = major, in the correctness lane.

finding.evidence: `const worksheet = unwrapJson<Worksheet>(root.sheets?.[tabId]);` — `unwrapJson` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:7-19) calls the proxy's `toJSON()` and then plain `JSON.parse`. Previous `unwrapJson` call sites only unwrapped small chart/image records; this is the first one that unwraps an entire user-authored grid.

verdict.reason: The code is present exactly as described. tabs.controller.ts:249 passes the whole live worksheet proxy (root.sheets[tabId], including the user-authored cell grid) through unwrapJson, and unwrapJson (yorkie-json.ts:7-19) does a bare JSON.parse of the proxy's toJSON() string with no repair and no try/catch. The same module documents and tests that Yorkie's raw JSON string path emits unescaped control characters inside string values, which is why parseJsonSnapshot/escapeControlCharsInJson (yorkie-json.ts:32-110) and the three-tier snapshotJsonRoot (yorkie-json.ts:173-205) exist, and document-copy.service.ts:498 uses the hardened path for whole-root user data. No guard makes the unhardened parse unreachable: the only preceding checks in the duplicate handler are the tab-existence check (tabs.controller.ts:245) and the post-hoc !worksheet check (line 250), neither of which catches a SyntaxError thrown inside unwrapJson, and nothing converts it to an HTTP error, so it escapes the withDocument callback as a 500. Reachable on a normal path (duplicating a tab whose cells hold control characters from paste/CSV import), so it is a correctness/crash defect in this lens, not out of scope. I could not read the installed SDK to confirm exactly which control characters Yorkie leaves unescaped, but that uncertainty concerns which input fires it, not whether the unhardened parse exists — under the rubric, that keeps the finding.

finding.evidence: `apply()` reads the deck (`readSlidesRoot(doc.getRoot())`), computes a new array outside `doc.update`, then assigns `root.slides = result.slides` wholesale. Yorkie resolves that as last-write-wins over the entire array, discarding any element/text change a collaborator committed on any slide in the interval. verdict.reason: The code is exactly as described: apply() reads a detached plain-JSON snapshot (readSlidesRoot -> unwrapJson, slides-tree.ts:52-81), rebuilds the entire slides array via MemSlidesStore (slide-ops.ts:78,95,115,131), and assigns it wholesale inside doc.update at slides.controller.ts:174-176. In Yorkie this is a last-write-wins set on the `slides` key, so element/text ops a collaborator commits against the prior array subtree are discarded, not merged. The window is genuine because YorkieService.withDocument attaches with SyncMode.Manual and only calls client.sync after the callback (yorkie.service.ts:50-60), so anything committed between snapshot and sync is superseded. The repo's own frontend store avoids exactly this by mutating in place with splice/property assignment specifically to preserve concurrent edits (yorkie-slides-store.ts:88, 734, 793, 803, 860), confirming the intended semantic. No guard, version check, or caller restriction makes this path unreachable; assertSlidesDocument only validates document type. Data loss of collaborator edits on a normally reachable REST path is squarely in the correctness lane and blocking at major severity.
